title: Human Resilience in the AI Era -- What Machines Can't Replace
abstract: arXiv:2510.25218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI is changing work and decision making faster than many institutions can adapt their operating practices. We argue that this adaptation gap makes human resilience a core capability for the AI era. We define resilience as the capacity to absorb disruption while preserving effective action and human agency around core purposes. The framework operates at three interacting levels. Psychological resilience keeps a person goal-directed under stress. Social resilience makes trusted support and correction available across a group. Organizational resilience turns detected problems into learning and recovery. We connect established resilience and technostress research with direct AI-in-the-loop experiments. General resilience is trainable, while AI-specific causal evidence is still emerging. Direct AI studies show that assistance can raise productivity and spread expertise. translated_title: 人工智能时代的人类韧性——机器无法替代的东西
translated_abstract: 人工智能正在以远超许多机构调整运营实践的速度改变着工作与决策方式。我们认为，这种适应差距使得人类韧性成为人工智能时代的一项核心能力。我们将韧性定义为：在吸收冲击的同时，仍能保持有效行动并围绕核心目标维持人类自主能动性的能力。该框架在三个相互作用的层面上运作：心理韧性使人在压力下保持目标导向；社会韧性使可信的支持与纠正能够在群体中获得；组织韧性将发现的问题转化为学习与恢复。我们将已有的韧性与技术压力研究同直接的“人机协作”实验联系起来。一般性韧性是可训练的，而针对AI的特异性因果证据仍在不断涌现。直接的AI研究显示，AI辅助能够提高生产力并促进专业知识的普及。其他实验则表明，AI能够提升表达出的共情能力，并使判断更加审慎校准。
tldr: 本文提出一个由心理、社会和组织三个交互层面构成的框架，论证在AI造成的“适应差距”背景下，人类韧性——即在冲击中保持有效行动与人类能动性的能力——是AI时代的核心能力，且这种能力是可训练的。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a three-level framework (psychological, social, and organizational resilience), arguing that amid the adaptation gap created by AI, human resilience—the capacity to absorb disruption while preserving effective action and human agency—is a trainable core capability for the AI era.
